source_evidence.observation: A_tilde is introduced as a p by p BLR representation of a dense matrix A. Diagonal blocks remain A_ii, off-diagonal b by b blocks are represented by rank-k_ij factors, n = pb, and k_ij is the least rank satisfying ||A_ij - A_tilde_ij|| <= epsilon beta_ij. Local and global choices are beta_ij = ||A_ij|| and beta_ij = ||A||. The unsubscripted norm is declared to be the Frobenius norm.

Each scalar operation satisfies fl(x op y) = (x op y)(1 + delta), |delta| <= u, for op in {+, -, multiplication, division}. The paper defines gamma_k = ku/(1-ku) when ku < 1 and permits non-integer gamma indices.

Computed truncated-SVD blocks satisfy A_tilde_ij = A_ij + Delta_A_ij with ||Delta_A_ij|| <= epsilon beta_ij. Rounding errors in these low-rank approximations are ignored, and the paper assumes throughout that u is safely smaller than epsilon.

source_evidence.anchor: Section 4 opening definition of BLR rank r
source_evidence.observation: The BLR rank is the largest off-diagonal block rank. In Section 4, r denotes the BLR rank of the computed LU factors, generally larger than the input matrix's BLR rank; r is not tunable and depends on the matrix and threshold.
Algorithm 1 is the UFC order: update, factor, then compress. Its factorization theorem assumes A is nonsingular, partitioned into p^2 blocks of order b, and that the algorithm runs to completion.

For UFC, the subsequent finite bound uses scaled thresholds. The scaled local choices divide ||A_ik|| by the relevant diagonal-factor norm and give xi_p = 1 without recompression; the scaled global choices divide ||A|| by that norm and give xi_p = p.

For UFC, A = L_tilde U_tilde + Delta_A with ||Delta_A|| <= (xi_p epsilon + gamma_p)||A|| + gamma_c||L_tilde||||U_tilde|| + O(u epsilon), where c = b + 2r^(3/2) + p. Table 1 gives xi_p as 1, p, p, and p^2/sqrt(6) for local/no-recompression, global/no-recompression, local/recompression, and global/recompression, respectively.

Algorithm 2 is the UCF order: update, compress, then factor. If it runs to completion on a nonsingular A partitioned into p^2 blocks of order b, it has the same displayed factorization bound and constant c as Theorem 4.2.
For UCF without recompression, ||G|| <= xi_p epsilon ||A|| with xi_p = 1 for beta_ik = ||A_ik|| and xi_p = p for beta_ik = ||A||. Unlike UFC, UCF does not require scaling by diagonal-factor norms.

A block triangular solve carried out by block substitution produces x_hat satisfying (T_tilde + Delta_T_tilde)x_hat = v + Delta_v, with ||Delta_T_tilde|| <= gamma_c||T_tilde|| and ||Delta_v|| <= gamma_p||v||, where this theorem's c is b + r^(3/2) + p.

The block solve uses x_i = x((i-1)b+1:ib) and the preceding-block sum j = 1,...,i-1. Theorem 4.5 states (A + Delta_A)x_hat = v + Delta_v, ||Delta_A|| <= (xi_p epsilon + gamma_p)||A|| + gamma_(3c)||L_tilde||||U_tilde|| + O(u epsilon), and ||Delta_v|| <= gamma_p(||v|| + ||L_tilde||||U_tilde||||x_hat||) + O(u^2), with c = b + 2r^(3/2) + p.

source_evidence.anchor: Proof of Theorem 4.5, exact perturbation composition
source_evidence.observation: Before simplification, the coefficient perturbation is the factorization perturbation plus Delta_L_tilde U_tilde, L_tilde Delta_U_tilde, and Delta_L_tilde Delta_U_tilde. The right-hand-side perturbation is the first-solve Delta_v plus L_tilde Delta_y_hat and Delta_L_tilde Delta_y_hat.

binders: Theorem 4.5 explicitly binds A_tilde in R^(n by n) as a pb by pb BLR matrix and v in R^n; the displayed system and conclusions instead use A. [PDF p. 24 (printed 974), anchor: Theorem 4.5 opening and equations (4.23)-(4.25)]
Section 2 supplies integers p and b with a p by p block partition, every block b by b, and n = pb. [PDF p. 3 (printed 953), anchor: equations (2.2)-(2.3)]

The inherited factorization results quantify a nonsingular A in R^(n by n), partitioned into p^2 blocks of order b. [PDF p. 19 (printed 969), anchor: Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 21 (printed 971), anchor: Theorem 4.3]

epsilon > 0 is the low-rank threshold, beta_ij selects the scale, u is the unit roundoff, and gamma_k = ku/(1-ku) where ku < 1. [PDF p. 3 (printed 953), anchor: equation (2.4); PDF p. 4 (printed 954), anchor: equation (2.5) and gamma definition]

L_tilde and U_tilde are computed BLR LU factors; y_hat and x_hat are the computed results of the two ordered triangular solves. [PDF p. 24 (printed 974), anchor: Theorem 4.5; PDF p. 25 (printed 975), anchor: proof of Theorem 4.5]
Delta_A in R^(n by n) and Delta_v in R^n are backward perturbations whose existence is asserted by equations (4.23)-(4.25). [PDF p. 24 (printed 974), anchor: equations (4.23)-(4.25)]
hypotheses: Explicit in Theorem 4.5: A_tilde is a real BLR matrix of the stated dimension and v is a real n-vector. [PDF p. 24 (printed 974), anchor: Theorem 4.5 opening]

Explicit in Theorem 4.5: the printed system Ax = v is solved by first solving L_tilde y = v and then U_tilde x = y, using factors computed by either Algorithm 1 or Algorithm 2. [PDF p. 24 (printed 974), anchor: Theorem 4.5 opening]

Inherited through Theorems 4.2 and 4.3: A is nonsingular, has p^2 blocks of order b, and the selected factorization algorithm runs to completion. [PDF p. 19 (printed 969), anchor: Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 21 (printed 971), anchor: Theorem 4.3]

Standing compression hypothesis: every truncated-SVD compression obeys ||A_tilde_ij - A_ij|| <= epsilon beta_ij, with its computation treated as free of additional rounding error. [PDF p. 5 (printed 955), anchor: Assumption 2.1]
Standing scale hypothesis: u is safely smaller than epsilon. [PDF p. 5 (printed 955), anchor: paragraph following Assumption 2.1]
The gamma quantities used by the bounds must lie in their declared domain ku < 1. [PDF p. 4 (printed 954), anchor: gamma definition following equation (2.5)]
conclusions: There are simultaneous coefficient and right-hand-side perturbations such that the computed solution obeys the exact relation (A + Delta_A)x_hat = v + Delta_v. [PDF p. 24 (printed 974), anchor: equation (4.23)]
The coefficient perturbation satisfies ||Delta_A|| <= (xi_p epsilon + gamma_p)||A|| + gamma_(3c)||L_tilde||||U_tilde|| + O(u epsilon). [PDF p. 24 (printed 974), anchor: equation (4.24)]

The right-hand-side perturbation satisfies ||Delta_v|| <= gamma_p(||v|| + ||L_tilde||||U_tilde||||x_hat||) + O(u^2). The factor-dependent term is inside the gamma_p parentheses. [PDF p. 24 (printed 974), anchor: equation (4.25)]
Here c = b + 2r^(3/2) + p and xi_p is selected from all four cases in Table 1. [PDF p. 24 (printed 974), anchor: text following equation (4.25); PDF p. 19 (printed 969), anchor: Table 1]
definitions_and_conventions: A_tilde represents a dense A blockwise: diagonal blocks remain A_ii, while off-diagonal blocks are low-rank approximations A_tilde_ij. [PDF p. 3 (printed 953), anchor: equations (2.2)-(2.3)]
For i > j, A_tilde_ij = X_ij Y_ij^T; for i < j, A_tilde_ij = Y_ij X_ij^T; X_ij and Y_ij are b by k_ij and X_ij has orthonormal columns. [PDF p. 3 (printed 953), anchor: equation (2.3)]
The rank k_ij is the minimum ell_ij for which rank(A_tilde_ij) = ell_ij and ||A_ij - A_tilde_ij|| <= epsilon beta_ij. [PDF p. 3 (printed 953), anchor: equation (2.4)]
The base local and global scales are beta_ij = ||A_ij|| and beta_ij = ||A||, respectively. [PDF p. 3 (printed 953), anchor: paragraph following equation (2.4)]

A hat denotes a computed solve result, while tildes denote BLR representations or computed BLR factors in the selected passage. [PDF p. 23 (printed 973), anchor: Theorem 4.4; PDF p. 24 (printed 974), anchor: Theorem 4.5]

The proof temporarily names the final composed perturbations Delta_A' and Delta_v'; these are the perturbations denoted Delta_A and Delta_v in the theorem statement. [PDF p. 25 (printed 975), anchor: final two displays in the proof of Theorem 4.5]
implicit_context: The nonsingularity and runs-to-completion conditions are not repeated in Theorem 4.5 but are inherited because its proof invokes Theorems 4.2 and 4.3. [PDF p. 24 (printed 974), anchor: first sentence of the proof of Theorem 4.5; PDF p. 19 (printed 969), anchor: Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 21 (printed 971), anchor: Theorem 4.3]

The triangular-solve perturbation result is inherited from Theorem 4.4, first for L_tilde and then 'similarly' for U_tilde. [PDF p. 25 (printed 975), anchor: first two displays in the proof of Theorem 4.5]

Theorem 4.4 itself uses c_tri = b + r^(3/2) + p; Theorem 4.5 uses the larger c = b + 2r^(3/2) + p when composing factorization and solve errors. [PDF p. 23 (printed 973), anchor: equation (4.21); PDF p. 24 (printed 974), anchor: text following equation (4.25)]

The paper's standing norm and floating-point conventions apply without being restated in Theorem 4.5. [PDF p. 3 (printed 953), anchor: Frobenius-norm paragraph; PDF p. 4 (printed 954), anchor: equation (2.5)]

No bounded-growth or stable-pivoting condition appears in the formal statement; possible factor growth remains visible through ||L_tilde||||U_tilde||. [PDF p. 24 (printed 974), anchor: equation (4.24)]
statement.algorithm_linkage: The permitted factorization executions are exactly Algorithm 1, UFC, and Algorithm 2, UCF. UFC performs update, factor, compress; UCF performs update, compress, factor. Both loop over k = 1,...,p and use update sums indexed j = 1,...,k-1. Theorem 4.5 then requires the ordered solves L_tilde y = v followed by U_tilde x = y. Run-to-completion is inherited from the factorization theorems. [PDF p. 13 (printed 963), anchor: Algorithm 1 and Theorem 4.1; PDF p. 21 (printed 971), anchor: Algorithm 2 and Theorem 4.3; PDF p. 24 (printed 974), anchor: Theorem 4.5]
numerical_model: The scalar model is fl(x op y) = (x op y)(1 + delta), |delta| <= u, for addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division. [PDF p. 4 (printed 954), anchor: equation (2.5)]
gamma_k means ku/(1-ku), is defined only for ku < 1, and may have a non-integer index. [PDF p. 4 (printed 954), anchor: gamma definition and following paragraph]

Low-rank truncated-SVD errors are modeled as deterministic normwise truncation errors bounded by epsilon beta_ij; rounding errors in the SVD compression itself are ignored. [PDF p. 5 (printed 955), anchor: Assumption 2.1]
The analysis assumes u is safely smaller than epsilon, so the low-rank and floating-point scales are distinct. [PDF p. 5 (printed 955), anchor: paragraph following Assumption 2.1]
error_notions: The result is a normwise backward-error statement with perturbations to both A and v, not a forward-error estimate for x_hat. [PDF p. 24 (printed 974), anchor: equations (4.23)-(4.25)]

The coefficient bound separates low-rank truncation, ordinary floating-point accumulation, factor-growth-dependent floating-point error, and a mixed higher-order term. [PDF p. 24 (printed 974), anchor: equation (4.24)]

The right-hand-side bound depends on v, the computed factors, and the computed x_hat; it is not merely a relative perturbation proportional to ||v||. [PDF p. 24 (printed 974), anchor: equation (4.25)]

The paper explicitly rejects a componentwise interpretation of low-rank approximation errors and conducts a normwise analysis. [PDF p. 3 (printed 953), anchor: paragraph preceding the Frobenius-norm convention]
norms: Every unsubscripted matrix norm in the analysis is the Frobenius norm. [PDF p. 3 (printed 953), anchor: Frobenius-norm convention]
For a block partition, ||A|| = (sum over i,j of ||A_ij||^2)^(1/2). [PDF p. 4 (printed 954), anchor: continuation of the Frobenius-norm convention]

The Frobenius norm is used as a submultiplicative norm and is invariant under left multiplication by a matrix with orthonormal columns. [PDF pp. 3-4 (printed 953-954), anchor: Frobenius-norm properties]

Applied to vectors v, x_hat, and Delta_v, the same unsubscripted convention is the Euclidean norm under the standard identification of vectors with one-column matrices. [PDF p. 3 (printed 953), anchor: declaration that the unsubscripted norm is used for all error analysis; PDF p. 24 (printed 974), anchor: equation (4.25)]
constants_and_indexing: The matrix has p block rows and p block columns, each block is b by b, and n = pb. [PDF p. 3 (printed 953), anchor: equations (2.2)-(2.3)]
r is the maximum off-diagonal block rank of the computed LU factors, not the input BLR rank and not a user-chosen rank cap. [PDF p. 12 (printed 962), anchor: opening definition of r]
Theorem 4.5 sets c = b + 2r^(3/2) + p and uses gamma_(3c) in the final coefficient perturbation. [PDF p. 24 (printed 974), anchor: equation (4.24) and following definition of c]

Table 1 gives xi_p = 1 for local/no recompression, xi_p = p for global/no recompression, xi_p = p for local/with recompression, and xi_p = p^2/sqrt(6) for global/with recompression. [PDF p. 19 (printed 969), anchor: Table 1]

For UFC, the finite xi_p values correspond to scaled local or global thresholds; for UCF, xi_p = 1 or p without recompression follows from the unscaled choices beta_ik = ||A_ik|| or beta_ik = ||A||. [PDF p. 17 (printed 967), anchor: equations (4.13)-(4.15); PDF p. 22 (printed 972), anchor: proof of Theorem 4.3]

The block triangular solve defines x_i = x((i-1)b+1:ib) and, for the displayed forward-substitution case, subtracts blocks j = 1,...,i-1. [PDF pp. 23-24 (printed 973-974), anchor: Theorem 4.4 and equation (4.22)]

Algorithm updates at factorization step k use previous factors with j = 1,...,k-1, including an empty update at k = 1. [PDF p. 12 (printed 962), anchor: description preceding Algorithm 1; PDF p. 13 (printed 963), anchor: Algorithm 1]
higher_order_terms: Equation (4.24) retains an unspecialized O(u epsilon) term; equation (4.25) separately retains O(u^2). Neither term may be deleted from the source contract. [PDF p. 24 (printed 974), anchor: equations (4.24)-(4.25)]

Using the proof's sign convention A + Delta_A_fac = L_tilde U_tilde, the exact composed coefficient perturbation before simplification is Delta_A_total = Delta_A_fac + Delta_L_tilde U_tilde + L_tilde Delta_U_tilde + Delta_L_tilde Delta_U_tilde. [PDF p. 25 (printed 975), anchor: first product expansion in the proof of Theorem 4.5]

The exact composed right-hand-side perturbation before simplification is Delta_v_total = Delta_v_L + L_tilde Delta_y_U + Delta_L_tilde Delta_y_U. [PDF p. 25 (printed 975), anchor: second product expansion in the proof of Theorem 4.5]

The factorization sub-bound already contains O(u epsilon), while products of solve perturbations contribute higher-order floating-point terms that are simplified into the theorem's displayed O terms. [PDF p. 24 (printed 974), anchor: first display in the proof of Theorem 4.5; PDF p. 25 (printed 975), anchor: final two bounds]
exceptional_values: The factorization must run to completion; this excludes algorithmic breakdown such as an unusable pivot in the chosen execution. [PDF p. 19 (printed 969), anchor: Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 21 (printed 971), anchor: Theorem 4.3]

Every gamma_k requires ku < 1; in particular the displayed final coefficient bound requires 3cu < 1 for gamma_(3c), and gamma_p requires pu < 1. [PDF p. 4 (printed 954), anchor: gamma definition; PDF p. 24 (printed 974), anchor: equations (4.24)-(4.25)]

The standing compression model requires epsilon > 0 and assumes u is safely smaller than epsilon. [PDF p. 3 (printed 953), anchor: equation (2.4); PDF p. 5 (printed 955), anchor: paragraph following Assumption 2.1]

Overflow, underflow, subnormal behavior, NaNs, and infinities are not addressed; the only stated arithmetic contract is the relative-error model (2.5). [PDF p. 4 (printed 954), anchor: equation (2.5)]

undebatable_constraints: The final exact relation perturbs both sides: (A + Delta_A)x_hat = v + Delta_v. [PDF p. 24 (printed 974), anchor: equation (4.23)]
The coefficient bound must contain the multiplier (xi_p epsilon + gamma_p)||A||, not xi_p epsilon by itself. [PDF p. 24 (printed 974), anchor: equation (4.24)]
The coefficient bound must use gamma_(3c)||L_tilde||||U_tilde|| with c = b + 2r^(3/2) + p. [PDF p. 24 (printed 974), anchor: equation (4.24) and following line]
The right-hand-side bound must place both ||v|| and ||L_tilde||||U_tilde||||x_hat|| inside the gamma_p factor. [PDF p. 24 (printed 974), anchor: equation (4.25)]
The matrix remainder is O(u epsilon), while the right-hand-side remainder is O(u^2). [PDF p. 24 (printed 974), anchor: equations (4.24)-(4.25)]

All norms are Frobenius norms under the paper's standing convention, and the result is normwise rather than componentwise. [PDF p. 3 (printed 953), anchor: normwise-analysis and Frobenius-norm paragraphs]
The only admitted factorization algorithms in Theorem 4.5 are Algorithm 1 UFC and Algorithm 2 UCF. [PDF p. 24 (printed 974), anchor: Theorem 4.5 opening]
The factors are computed BLR factors, and x_hat is obtained through two ordered computed triangular solves. [PDF pp. 24-25 (printed 974-975), anchor: Theorem 4.5 and its proof]
The four possible xi_p values and their threshold/recompression cases must all be preserved. [PDF p. 19 (printed 969), anchor: Table 1]
r refers to the BLR rank of the computed factors and must not be replaced by the input matrix's BLR rank. [PDF p. 12 (printed 962), anchor: opening definition of r]

Nonsingularity and runs-to-completion are inherited prerequisites of the factorization results used in the proof. [PDF p. 19 (printed 969), anchor: Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 21 (printed 971), anchor: Theorem 4.3]

No theorem-level assumption permits replacing the factor norm product by a constant; any stability interpretation must retain ||L_tilde||||U_tilde|| unless an additional growth assumption is supplied. [PDF p. 24 (printed 974), anchor: equation (4.24)]

ambiguities.issue: Theorem 4.5 explicitly quantifies A_tilde but then states and proves conclusions about A.
ambiguities.evidence: The opening says 'Let A_tilde in R^(n by n) be a pb by pb BLR matrix', while the same sentence uses Ax = v and equations (4.23)-(4.24) use A. Section 2 defines A_tilde as a BLR representation of dense A. [PDF p. 24 (printed 974), anchor: Theorem 4.5 opening and equations (4.23)-(4.24); PDF p. 3 (printed 953), anchor: equation (2.2)]
ambiguities.impact: A faithful contract must preserve the printed A in the system and perturbation bounds. Replacing it by A_tilde, or adding a specific global relation between A and A_tilde, requires an interpretation not explicitly stated in Theorem 4.5.

ambiguities.issue: Table 1 labels thresholds only as local or global, but UFC and UCF reach those coefficients with different threshold scaling conventions.
ambiguities.evidence: The UFC discussion says subsequent results use scaled thresholds and Corollary 4.1 identifies xi_p = 1 or p for scaled local or global thresholds. The UCF proof derives the same values from unscaled beta_ik = ||A_ik|| or ||A|| and explicitly says UCF need not scale. [PDF p. 17 (printed 967), anchor: equations (4.13)-(4.15); PDF p. 22 (printed 972), anchor: proof and discussion following Theorem 4.3; PDF p. 19 (printed 969), anchor: Table 1]
ambiguities.impact: An implementation-level formalization must associate xi_p with both the algorithm and its threshold convention; the words 'local' and 'global' alone do not fully specify the UFC execution.

ambiguities.issue: The constants and dimensional scales hidden by O(u epsilon) and O(u^2) are not specified.
ambiguities.evidence: The theorem and proof leave these terms in big-O form without defining their hidden constants or dependencies. [PDF pp. 24-25 (printed 974-975), anchor: equations (4.24)-(4.25) and final proof bounds]
ambiguities.impact: The passage supports asymptotic remainder terms, not a completely explicit finite inequality for those contributions.

ambiguities.issue: The standing phrase that u is 'safely smaller' than epsilon is qualitative.
ambiguities.evidence: After Assumption 2.1 the paper states that the assumption is satisfied only if u is safely smaller than epsilon and adopts this throughout, but gives no numerical separation factor. [PDF p. 5 (printed 955), anchor: paragraph following Assumption 2.1]
ambiguities.impact: A formal statement cannot substitute a particular inequality such as u <= epsilon/2 without adding information not present in the paper.

ambiguities.issue: The upper-triangular solve's block indexing is not restated.
ambiguities.evidence: Theorem 4.4 explicitly displays forward block substitution with j = 1,...,i-1. In the proof of Theorem 4.5, the U_tilde solve is introduced only with 'Similarly'. [PDF pp. 23-24 (printed 973-974), anchor: Theorem 4.4 and equation (4.22); PDF p. 25 (printed 975), anchor: second display in the proof of Theorem 4.5]
ambiguities.impact: Backward substitution is the evident intended analogue, but its exact index order is inherited rather than explicitly written in the selected theorem.

ambiguities.issue: The pivoting strategy is not fixed by the theorem.
ambiguities.evidence: Algorithms 1 and 2 do not specify a pivoting rule; their formal hypotheses require only nonsingularity and running to completion. The UCF discussion notes complications for standard pivoting strategies. [PDF p. 13 (printed 963), anchor: Algorithm 1 and Theorem 4.1; PDF p. 21 (printed 971), anchor: discussion preceding Theorem 4.3 and Algorithm 2]
ambiguities.impact: The theorem gives a conditional backward bound containing factor growth. It does not by itself justify replacing that factor-growth term by a modest universal constant.

ambiguities.issue: Floating-point exceptional behavior is outside the stated model.
ambiguities.evidence: Equation (2.5) gives only a relative-error model for the four basic operations and contains no clauses for overflow, underflow, subnormals, NaNs, or infinities. [PDF p. 4 (printed 954), anchor: equation (2.5)]
ambiguities.impact: Those exceptional cases must be excluded or handled by an additional model; the paper passage does not determine their behavior.

contract_plain_english: Under the paper's standing Frobenius-norm compression and floating-point models, take the block matrix associated with A, compute BLR factors by either the UFC or UCF algorithm under the inherited nonsingularity and runs-to-completion conditions, solve L_tilde y = v and then U_tilde x = y, and call the computed result x_hat. [PDF pp. 19, 21, and 24 (printed 969, 971, and 974), anchors: Theorems 4.2, 4.3, and 4.5] Then x_hat exactly solves a jointly perturbed system (A + Delta_A)x_hat = v + Delta_v, where ||Delta_A|| <= (xi_p epsilon + gamma_p)||A|| + gamma_(3c)||L_tilde||||U_tilde|| + O(u epsilon) and ||Delta_v|| <= gamma_p(||v|| + ||L_tilde||||U_tilde||||x_hat||) + O(u^2), with c = b + 2r^(3/2) + p. [PDF p. 24 (printed 974), anchor: equations (4.23)-(4.25)] Here r is the maximum off-diagonal rank of the computed factors, and xi_p is 1, p, p, or p^2/sqrt(6) according to the local/global and without/with-recompression cases in Table 1. [PDF p. 12 (printed 962), anchor: definition of r; PDF p. 19 (printed 969), anchor: Table 1] The theorem's printed mismatch between the bound variable A and the explicitly introduced A_tilde remains unresolved except for Section 2's convention that A_tilde is a BLR representation of dense A. [PDF p. 3 (printed 953), anchor: equation (2.2); PDF p. 24 (printed 974), anchor: Theorem 4.5]
